title: Peking Duck

seo.title: How to Make Peking Duck — Easy Chinese Recipe
seo.metaDescription: Learn how to make authentic Peking Duck. This easy Chinese recipe includes step-by-step instructions, tips, and serving ideas.
h2Headings: Pro Tips for the Best Results
seo.imageCaption: Delicious homemade Peking Duck — a beloved Chinese classic

description: Peking Duck is a legendary dish known for its irresistibly crispy skin and succulent, flavorful meat. This iconic Chinese delicacy is often served with thin pancakes, scallions, and hoisin sauce, creating a delightful culinary experience. Preparing it at home allows you to savor the rich traditions and incredible taste of this beloved classic.

instructions.title: Prepare the Duck
instructions.text: Thoroughly clean the duck inside and out, removing any excess fat or giblets. Pat the duck extremely dry with paper towels. Combine five-spice powder and salt, then rub this mixture all over the duck, inside and out. Place the duck on a rack set over a baking sheet.

instructions.title: Apply the Glaze
instructions.text: In a saucepan, combine honey (or maltose), rice vinegar, Shaoxing wine, and water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 2 minutes until slightly thickened. Carefully pour or brush this hot glaze evenly over the entire duck. Ensure all skin is coated.

instructions.title: Dry the Duck Skin
instructions.text: Place the glazed duck in the refrigerator, uncovered, for at least 4 hours or preferably overnight. This crucial step allows the skin to dry out, which is key to achieving that signature crispiness. If possible, use a fan to circulate air around the duck for even better drying.

instructions.title: Roast the Duck
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). Place the duck on a rack in a roasting pan, breast-side up. Add about 1 inch of water to the bottom of the roasting pan to keep the duck moist and prevent drippings from burning. Roast for 1 hour, then reduce the oven temperature to 325°F (160°C) and continue roasting for another 45 minutes to 1 hour, or until an internal temperature of 165°F (74°C) is reached in the thickest part of the thigh.

instructions.title: Rest and Carve
instructions.text: Once cooked, remove the duck from the oven and let it rest on a cutting board for at least 15-20 minutes. This allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring a tender and flavorful duck. Carefully carve the crispy skin into small squares or strips, then slice the meat from the duck.

instructions.title: Serve Peking Duck
instructions.text: Arrange the carved duck skin and meat on a platter. Serve immediately with warm thin pancakes or steamed buns, hoisin sauce, julienned scallions, and cucumber strips. Each person can assemble their own wrap by spreading hoisin on a pancake, adding duck, scallions, and cucumber.

tips: The drying process is absolutely critical for crispy skin. Do not skip or shorten this step. Using a fan can significantly improve the crispiness.
For an even richer flavor, you can stuff the duck cavity with aromatics like ginger, scallions, and star anise before roasting.
Warm the pancakes or buns just before serving by steaming them for a few minutes. This makes them soft and pliable for wrapping.
